name: Brow slitting / cuts

lead: Brow slitting is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines of hair are shaved out of the eyebrow so bare skin shows through, giving an edgy, distinctive look. The change is visible at once.

It is a styling choice rather than a structural change: hair is trimmed or shaved from a narrow strip with a razor or trimmer, and nothing is done to the follicle, so the gap grows back. It has been popular with some young people since at least the 1990s. Little scientific material exists on it, and no studies have tested its effect on how a face is perceived.

paras: People use a razor or trimmer, often at a barber, to cut a slit, and redo it as the hair regrows over a few weeks. It is commonly paired with a matching haircut or streetwear style.

Shaving carries the usual minor risks of razor use such as nicks or irritation. A 2008 news report cited by Wikipedia linked the style to gang concerns in some schools, which can matter where school or workplace dress rules apply.

angle.text: Users shave one or more thin slits through the eyebrow as a streetwear-style statement. The gap shows bare skin through the brow right away and grows back with time.

lead: Brow slitting, also called eyebrow slits or eyebrow cuts, is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines are shaved or trimmed through the eyebrow hair so that a bare strip of skin shows as a short vertical or diagonal gap. People use it as a styling accent: the gap draws attention to the brow and eye area and gives the face a deliberate, edgy look. It is done with a razor or trimmer and does not involve cutting skin.

The style is generally traced to hip-hop in the late 1980s, where Big Daddy Kane is widely named as an early popular wearer, followed by Kriss Kross, Vanilla Ice and, later, Bow Wow and Soulja Boy.[1][2][3] It has returned to fashion several times, including on the Miu Miu spring-summer 2021 runway, and is worn by athletes and pop stars such as Neymar Jr and members of BTS.[2]
Wikipedia's article on eyebrows notes that shaving lines into the eyebrows was a cosmetic trend among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s.[4] No published studies have examined the style.
infobox: Hair shaved or trimmed from the brow

paras: The style removes a narrow strip of hair across the brow, most often near the tail or arch, leaving a visible gap. Variations include a single slit, multiple slits, or a diagonal cut; people in the 2015 revival tried one to three cuts in one or both brows.[1] Complex notes that hip-hop communities call these "cuts" and objected to the term "slits".[1]

Complex, citing The Root, traces the look to Big Daddy Kane, and a 2015 article lists Soulja Boy and Bow Wow among its wearers; Jay-Z referenced it on his 1999 song "Do It Again (Put Ya Hands Up)".[1] Another history says Kane wore several cuts in the late 1980s and that Kriss Kross, Vanilla Ice, Luke Perry as Dylan in Beverly Hills 90210, and David Beckham in the early 2000s also wore them.[2] Its roots are described as unclear, and one account speculates it echoes real scars from fights.[2]

In 2015 BuzzFeed reported the trend returning, with Instagram posts under the hashtag #EyebrowSlits.[1] In December 2017 Toronto beauty blogger Menal Khan posted a version she called "boxed brows", which Huda Kattan reposted; Yahoo Life traced it to earlier hip-hop style and noted she did not credit that source.[3]

Miu Miu's spring-summer 2021 show featured models with two cuts in one brow, and Isamaya Ffrench created a similar gapped effect with brow concealer for Poster Girl spring-summer 2023.[2] Wearers named include Neymar Jr, BTS, Zayn Malik and Jason Momoa, whose cut is a real scar.[2]

Brow shaping is long established, and fashions have changed repeatedly: Japanese hikimayu from the 8th century involved shaving or plucking brows and painting them higher on the forehead, Elizabethan high-status women sometimes removed brows entirely, and thin plucked brows returned in the 1920s and 1930s.[4] Modern options include tweezing, waxing, threading, trimming, makeup, microblading and transplants.[4]
Wikipedia describes the brows as important to communication, since mobile brows convey emotions such as surprise, recognition and sympathy.[4]

In some communities the cuts have also signalled gang affiliation, according to Yahoo Life, and Wikipedia mentions a 2008 news report connecting shaved brow lines to gang-related concerns in schools.[4][3] Other coverage treats the cuts mainly as a style choice tied to hip-hop and barbershop design culture, in which intricate clipper work has long been common.[1][3]

Brow slits are generally treated in appearance communities as a style choice rather than a facial-structure change. Discussion of eyebrows in these spaces more often concerns shape, density and the eye area.
